default: Review recent requests from the same IP/user/tenant around this timestamp
Apply temporary rate-limiting or blocking on the offending IP/user/tenant
Correlate with application / infra logs to confirm whether the action succeeded

SQL Injection: [Immediate Action] Temporarily block suspicious IPs/users in WAF or reverse proxy
[Immediate Action] Check DB logs and recent queries for data exfiltration or schema tampering
[Short-term] Fix the specific endpoint to use parameterized queries (no string concatenation)
[Short-term] Disable verbose SQL error messages in production
[Long-term] Add automated SQLi tests to CI and keep WAF rules for injection attacks enabled
NoSQL Injection: [Immediate Action] Review recent requests to the affected endpoint, look for payloads with $where/$ne/$gt etc.
[Immediate Action] Block or rate-limit offending IPs/users at the edge/WAF
[Short-term] Sanitize and validate fields passed into NoSQL queries (block operators in user input)
[Short-term] Disable server-side eval / JavaScript execution in the NoSQL engine if possible
[Long-term] Introduce an allowlist of queryable fields and enforce strict schema validation
LDAP Injection: [Immediate Action] Review authentication / directory access logs for unusual LDAP filter patterns
[Immediate Action] Block suspicious IPs or accounts abusing the login / directory endpoints
[Short-term] Escape all user-controlled input in LDAP filters or use parameterized directory APIs
[Short-term] Restrict LDAP account used by the app to least-privilege (no wildcard searches)
[Long-term] Add tests for LDAP injection patterns and log all failed bind/search attempts with context
Command Injection: [Immediate Action] Immediately review logs for spawned shell commands / abnormal child processes on the host
[Immediate Action] Isolate or restart affected pod/host if you see suspicious shells or outbound connections
[Short-term] Remove shell invocation (shell=True) and use safe APIs without passing raw strings
[Short-term] Strictly validate/allowlist input before passing it to any OS-level tool
[Long-term] Add host-level monitoring (EDR, auditd) for suspicious process trees and outbound traffic
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): [Immediate Action] Identify vulnerable parameter/field and block or sanitize it server-side
[Immediate Action] Check for active malicious content stored in DB (comments, profiles, messages) and clean it up
[Short-term] Apply output encoding for all untrusted data in HTML/JS/attributes
[Short-term] Set Content-Security-Policy (CSP) and HttpOnly/SameSite flags on cookies
[Long-term] Introduce secure templating / component libraries and add XSS tests to CI
Cross-Site Request Forgery: [Immediate Action] Confirm whether the endpoint changes state (transfers, profile changes, admin actions)
[Immediate Action] Identify if the endpoint is missing CSRF protection and restrict it temporarily if needed
[Short-term] Enable CSRF tokens or same-site cookie protections for state-changing endpoints
[Short-term] Require re-auth or step-up auth for sensitive actions (transfers, password change)
[Long-term] Review all state-changing routes for proper CSRF and add regression tests
Server-Side Request Forgery: [Immediate Action] Inspect logs for outbound HTTP calls to internal IP ranges and metadata services
[Immediate Action] Block suspicious IPs/users and disable the vulnerable fetch/proxy endpoint if required
[Short-term] Introduce allowlist of outbound destinations for server-side HTTP clients
[Short-term] Block access to RFC1918 ranges and link-local addresses at network/WAF level
[Long-term] Add SSRF-specific tests and harden internal services that should never be reachable
Cloud Metadata SSRF: [Immediate Action] Immediately check cloud metadata/IMDS audit logs for token/credential access around this time
[Immediate Action] Rotate any potentially exposed instance / workload credentials
[Short-term] Block metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254, metadata.*) at host or VPC firewall level
[Short-term] Enforce IMDSv2 / metadata auth headers where supported (AWS/GCP/Azure)
[Long-term] Reduce IAM permissions for instance roles and add monitoring for metadata access anomalies
API Key Exposure: [Immediate Action] Revoke or rotate the exposed API key / token immediately
[Immediate Action] Search application logs, tickets and repos for the same key re-use
[Short-term] Replace hard-coded secrets with a secrets manager (Vault, KMS, etc.)
[Short-term] Add secret-scanning to CI/CD and pre-commit hooks
[Long-term] Enforce key scoping and expiry, and monitor usage for anomalies on regenerated keys
Sensitive Data Exposure: [Immediate Action] Determine what data was actually exposed (PII, credentials, financial, internal docs)
[Immediate Action] Remove or redact sensitive payloads from logs, tickets, and monitoring systems
[Short-term] Encrypt sensitive data at rest and in transit; mask it in logs and analytics
[Short-term] Add access controls / row-level security where applicable
[Long-term] Classify data and enforce DLP policies plus continuous monitoring for leaks
Authentication Brute-Force: [Immediate Action] Enable or tighten login rate limits and lockout policies for affected accounts/IP ranges
[Immediate Action] Check for any successful logins from the attacking IPs or suspicious geo/ASN
[Short-term] Enforce MFA on high-value accounts and admin users
[Short-term] Add CAPTCHA / bot protection on login and password reset flows
[Long-term] Correlate brute-force attempts with credential stuffing and add anomaly detection rules
Credential Stuffing: [Immediate Action] Check whether suspicious logins re-used known breached passwords or combos
[Immediate Action] Force password reset / session revocation for impacted accounts
[Short-term] Integrate with breached password checks (HaveIBeenPwned or similar)
[Short-term] Add device / IP reputation and risk-based authentication
[Long-term] Promote passwordless / WebAuthn for critical users and monitor for reuse across tenants
Broken Access Control (IDOR): [Immediate Action] Identify which objects/tenants could be accessed by an unauthorized user
[Immediate Action] Invalidate any exposed session tokens and check access logs for mass-enumeration patterns
[Short-term] Enforce per-object authorization checks on the vulnerable endpoints
[Short-term] Replace sequential IDs with opaque surrogates where possible
[Long-term] Introduce systematic access-control layer and tests for every read/update/delete route
Security Misconfiguration: [Immediate Action] Disable debug endpoints, directory listings and stack traces in production
[Immediate Action] Remove default credentials and test accounts from exposed services
[Short-term] Align environment configs (prod/stage/dev) with hardened baselines
[Short-term] Enable security headers (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, CSP, etc.)
[Long-term] Automate config checks (CIS benchmarks, scanners) and enforce them in CI/CD
Denial of Service: [Immediate Action] Confirm if the service is currently degraded and enable stronger rate limits on hot endpoints
[Immediate Action] Identify top offending IPs/ASNs and block at WAF / edge if needed
[Short-term] Add timeouts, circuit breakers, and backpressure on expensive operations
[Short-term] Introduce per-tenant quotas and prioritise critical traffic
[Long-term] Plan capacity / autoscaling and add anomaly detection on traffic patterns
WebSocket Abuse: [Immediate Action] Review recent WebSocket connections from the offending IP/user and terminate abusive sessions
[Immediate Action] Tighten rate limits for messages, connections and rooms/channels
[Short-term] Enforce authentication and authorization on WS upgrades and subscription events
[Short-term] Restrict allowed origins and subprotocols for WebSocket endpoints
[Long-term] Add monitoring for WS message volume, fan-out abuse and suspicious broadcast patterns
Business Logic Abuse: [Immediate Action] Identify whether any financial/critical operations (refunds, discounts, transfers) were exploited
[Immediate Action] Temporarily disable or constrain the abused action (coupon, refund, price change) if feasible
[Short-term] Implement idempotency keys and server-side checks to prevent duplicates and races
[Short-term] Add validation on business rules (limits, thresholds, ownership checks) on the backend
[Long-term] Threat-model critical flows (checkout, refunds, payouts) and add abuse-focused test cases
